governor.title: Governor and Lieutenant Governor
governor.one: The governor runs the state, writes the first draft of the state budget, and signs or vetoes every bill the legislature passes. The lieutenant governor takes over if the governor can't serve and leads the State Senate.
governor.why: Shapes how New York spends its money on schools, transit, housing, and health care.
also: You vote for the governor and lieutenant governor together, as a pair
Can veto single items out of the budget

ag.title: Attorney General
ag.one: New York's top lawyer. Represents the state in court.
ag.why: Goes after scams, landlords and employers who break the law, and companies that mislead customers.
also: Can win refunds for people who got ripped off

comptroller.title: Comptroller
comptroller.one: The state's money watchdog. Checks how state agencies and local governments spend money, and runs the state workers' pension fund.
comptroller.why: Catches waste and fraud with your tax dollars.
also: Reviews big state contracts before they can be signed

house.title: U.S. House
house.one: Votes on national laws, and speaks for your district in Washington.
house.why: Your closest voice in Washington, and you get to keep or replace them every two years.

sen.title: State Senate
sen.one: Writes New York's laws and passes the state budget. There are 63 state senators.
sen.why: State laws cover schools, rent rules, voting rules, criminal law, and state taxes.

asm.title: State Assembly
asm.one: The other half of the legislature. There are 150 Assembly members, each with a smaller district than a senator's.
asm.why: Every bill has to pass here and in the State Senate before the governor can sign it.
